name: Playground / 真实流式对话 / 部署入口、网关 SSE、刷新持久化与新对话隔离
scope: Single targeted contract; not a full Playground or renderer completion claim
identity: admin browser session; node agent/Docker; the Playground calls /api/v1/playground/v1/* with the session, not an inference key
fixture: isolated server, fresh SQLite, unique runId, real Chrome (two browser contexts), real agent over WS, real Docker daemon; GPU facts injected for scheduling only; engine is the audited fake-engine image

execution_evidence.reason: The Playground streamed two real requests through the gateway to the fake-engine container; the SSE bodies carried the engine marker and [DONE], and the UI rendered the replies. The deployment container stayed running.

crud.create: covered: a conversation is created by sending the first message and appears in the sidebar
crud.read: covered: messages render, survive a reload, and reopen from the sidebar
crud.delete: MISSING: conversation deletion and the retention cap

covered: the deployment's openai.chat operation enables the button
the URL carries operation=openai.chat and the served model
the served name is listed by the Playground catalog and selected
missing: the disabled entry before the runtime is ready

covered: a prompt is sent unchanged in a streaming chat body
SSE content deltas contain the engine marker
the reply renders and the stop button clears
missing: SSE error events and usage details

covered: the first prompt becomes the conversation title
a reload keeps the conversation and its messages
a new conversation starts empty and the sidebar shows both
switching back restores the first conversation only
a fresh browser context has no conversations
each fresh conversation sends exactly one user message with its own prompt, model and stream flag
missing: two accounts on the same browser and their isolation
rename, delete and the retention cap

partial_checklist.20.6: History is now shown to be keyed to the signed-in account inside one browser: after logging out and back in the same browser shows both conversations again and the store holds every row under a single positive account key, while a separate browser context starts empty. What still holds the item at partial is real cross-account isolation: this product exposes one admin account and no user management, so a second account cannot be created through the product. I tried to prove the check by making the store ignore the account key and return every row - it did not fail, because with a single account the result is identical. That is a gap in what this environment can prove, not evidence of isolation, so it stays open rather than being claimed.
partial_checklist.20.3: Chunking, the terminal [DONE] event, error events and usage are now asserted separately from the reply text, and the reply shows the reported token count exactly instead of an approximation, so a reply that ignores its usage event is caught (killed by dropping the recorded usage: the metric turns into ≈1). What still holds the item at partial is cancellation: at this stream shape the stop control is gone before it can be clicked, and holding the reply open changed the timing the completed-reply assertions depend on.

missing: Streaming cancellation, upstream termination and interrupted-reply marking
Gateway error paths (unknown model, unauthorized key, engine failure/429)
Conversation rename/delete, retention cap and multi-account isolation
The other locale (each run covers one --locale)

fault_runs.name: playground-route-all-chat

mutation.intent: route every operation to the chat page

fault_runs.review_note: Killed at the renderer assertion: the mutant sends embeddings to /playground/chat, so the expected /playground/vector URL never appears. Reaching the pages through the product's own operation links is what makes this a real detector; navigating to a hand-built URL passed under the mutant and proved nothing.

checklist_items.20.1: The deployment declares chat, embeddings and rerank; opening an operation the model does not declare lists the declared ones, and each link opens its own renderer: chat -> /playground/chat, embeddings and rerank -> /playground/vector. Nothing degrades to chat. Verified en+zh; killed by routing every operation to chat, after which embeddings arrives at /playground/chat instead of /playground/vector.
checklist_items.20.2: Each declared operation sends its own method, path and body and returns its own business result: chat streams SSE to [DONE] with the engine marker, embeddings POSTs {input} to the gateway's /v1/embeddings and returns one numeric vector, rerank POSTs {query, documents} to /v1/rerank and returns indexed relevance scores in descending order with no chat wire reuse. Verified en+zh.
checklist_items.20.9: Both credential planes are exercised and proved not to substitute for each other. An inference key copied from the UI reaches the public /v1/models with Bearer only and no cookies (200), while the signed-in browser session gets 401 there and the inference key gets 401 on the session path /api/v1/playground/models; the key keeps authenticating its own path afterwards. Revoking the key returns it to 401 while the guard key still authenticates. Verified en+zh; killed by letting the public gateway accept the session cookie, after which the session reached /v1/models with 200.
checklist_items.20.7: A reply's HTML block is opened through the product's own preview button and the generated page really runs. Its frame carries sandbox "allow-scripts allow-modals allow-downloads" with no allow-same-origin, so the page sits in an opaque origin: it reports window.origin as null and reading the console location raises SecurityError, while the product's in-memory storage stand-in keeps localStorage usable. Under the restrictive policy the document carries the CSP with connect-src 'none', and the page's http(s) open request becomes a confirmation carrying the URL instead of navigating the frame. Verified en+zh. Two mutants were killed: dropping the CSP injection ('CSP presence does not match allow_network=False') and adding allow-same-origin to the sandbox ('the preview sandbox was granted the console origin').
checklist_items.20.8: The administrator's security setting decides the preview's network policy end to end. The settings page's playground_preview_network switch was flipped through the UI and saved, the stored policy changed false->true, and the next preview carried no CSP while the sandbox string stayed byte-identical, so allowing the network never grants the console origin; the setting was then restored through the same switch and re-read from the API. Verified en+zh. Killed by the same two mutants as 20.7, which both fail the restricted-policy run.

fault_runs.name: playground-usage-event-dropped

mutation.intent: the product keeps receiving the usage event but no longer records it

fault_runs.review_note: Killed at the token metric: the reply shows ≈1 instead of the reported 8, so a reply that ignores its usage event cannot pass. Mutating the gateway's include_usage injection instead did NOT kill anything, because the fake engine reports usage unconditionally; that attempt is recorded as an equivalent mutation rather than counted.

fault_runs.name: gateway-accepts-session-cookie

mutation.intent: let a signed-in browser session authenticate the public Bearer path

fault_runs.review_note: Killed at the plane-separation assertion: the browser session got 200 on /v1/models, so one credential standing in for the other cannot pass.

undetected_mutation.intent: list() ignores the account key and returns every stored conversation
undetected_mutation.why: A single admin account means the leaked result equals the correct one, so this test cannot distinguish them. Recorded as an environment limitation, not as a proven property.

fault_runs.name: csp-removed

mutation.intent: stop injecting the restricted CSP into the preview document

fault_runs.review_note: Killed at 'CSP presence does not match allow_network=False', so a preview that silently loses its policy cannot pass.

fault_runs.name: same-origin-granted
fault_runs.review_note: Killed at 'the preview sandbox was granted the console origin', so the origin isolation is asserted, not just the CSP.
